title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
title_zh: MARQ：融合系统工程知识的模块化、LLM 无关的需求质量评估器

paragraphs.en: MARQ通过注入系统工程知识评估需求质量，在多个LLM上显著提升缺陷检出且模型无关。 Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. This study investigates whether infusing expert-derived SE knowledge can improve LLM-based requirement quality evaluation beyond off-the-shelf capability. We present MARQ, a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype that supplements LLMs with a criterion-specific knowledge stack operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria and evaluated against off-the-shelf baselines on an expert-labeled NASA requirement set using Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the open-weight Gemma 3 12B, with 100 executions per model. MARQ achieves median F1 scores of 0.80 for Claude Opus 5, 0.62 for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 0.53 for Gemma 3 12B, compared with off-the-shelf baselines of 0.55, 0.52, and 0.18, respectively. However, the nature of these gains is model-dependent. Claude Opus 5 improves defect detection and false-alarm control; GPT-5.6 Sol gains detection and better execution-level consistency at the cost of more false alarms; and Gemma 3 12B reaches the performance of off-the-shelf proprietary models, although it remains highly variable. Criterion-level analysis shows gains concentrated in Correctness and Conformance, trade-offs between misses and false alarms within individual criteria, and model-dependent responses across several criteria. These findings position SE knowledge infusion as a promising model-agnostic pathway for strengthening trustworthy LLM-based RE support while underscoring the need for criterion-specific interventions and human-in-the-loop review.
paragraphs.zh: MARQ通过注入系统工程知识评估需求质量，在多个LLM上显著提升缺陷检出且模型无关。需求工程（RE）是系统工程（SE）的基础，因为需求缺陷会向下游传播并对开发结果产生不利影响。 尽管大型语言模型（LLM）在需求质量评估方面很有前景，但已有研究表明，开箱即用的模型会遗漏大量专家识别出的缺陷，在不同质量准则上表现不均衡，且多次执行之间结果不一。 本研究探讨注入源自专家的SE知识能否提升基于LLM的需求质量评估，使其超越开箱即用的能力。 我们提出MARQ，一个模块化、模型无关的原型系统，它通过一个针对具体准则的知识栈为LLM补充知识，该知识栈将INCOSE需求质量准则付诸实施，并在专家标注的NASA需求集上以Claude Opus 5、GPT-5.6 Sol和开放权重的Gemma 3 12B（每个模型执行100次）与开箱即用的基线进行了对比评估。 与开箱即用基线的0.55、0.52和0.18相比，MARQ的中位数F1分数分别为：Claude Opus 5达到0.80，GPT-5.6 Sol达到0.62，Gemma 3 12B达到0.53。 然而，这些提升的性质依赖于具体模型。 Claude Opus 5改善了缺陷检出和误报控制；GPT-5.6 Sol在检出能力和执行层面一致性上有所提升，但代价是误报增多；Gemma 3 12B达到了开箱即用专有模型的性能水平，尽管其表现仍高度不稳定。 准则层面的分析表明，提升集中在正确性与符合性上，各准则内部存在漏检与误报之间的权衡，且在若干准则上模型的响应因模型而异。 这些发现将SE知识注入定位为一条有前景的模型无关路径，可用于强化可信的基于LLM的RE支持，同时强调了针对具体准则的干预措施和人机协同评审的必要性。
